title: Why he lets others pick his sidemen
summary: He stopped choosing musicians because they develop his ideas and leave; he names several drummers he worked with.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: No, I let them do all the picking. I let them do all the picking. I let them do all the picking. Just like it is now with me with Quince. I don't pick them because it's a headache. I got tired of that many years ago. You know, first of all you pick a guy and he develops what you're trying to learn, and he don't never stay no way. They get ideas of their own. It ain't waste teaching to show it nobody, not in the field in that manner, you know. Smokey Johnson, and Honey Boy, oh I can name a bunch of them, you know, Drummer, Sheva, all of them, you know.
Yeah, well you work with Honey Boy, I know. Yeah. Tali Otis, this is me.
Try to help them buy instruments and all, and so as they get a break, some other place, they're gone, you know.
